title: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource Settings

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model robustness and performance across different writing systems (native Ge'ez script versus improvised Romanized Latin transliterations) to ensure the models accurately represent and process actual sociolinguistic usage in low-resource settings.
Measuring classification bias by analyzing per-class F1 scores to identify model performance disparities and failure rates in correctly detecting sexist abusive content.
Evaluating algorithmic classification bias by comparing per-class F1 scores to detect performance disparities in identifying racially abusive content compared to majority topics.
Assessing classification imbalances and performance variance by tracking F1 scores to identify systemic failures in recognizing religious abuse.
Measuring model performance on political topics relative to other sensitive minority classes to evaluate domain-specific classification imbalances.
